licence_note: Text-free: question ids, counts, mechanisms, flag and screen names. No LoCoMo/OP-Bench text, quotes or speaker names.

honest_headline.note: 81.4% raw becomes about 80.5% (79.1-81.7) after hand-read judge errors in both directions; multi-hop 66.7% raw becomes about 61.1% central. Shift is inside the bootstrap CI but concentrated in multi-hop.

proposed_screens_note: S79-S100 are proposals, not queued; S68-S78 belong to OBS-GAPS (provisional).

items.title: Multi-evidence recall: fixed depth, no coverage objective, weak aggregation trigger
items.problem: Questions that need three or more independent evidence items (list, count, 'all', 'both') get a fixed top-k anchor set. The chance that every needed item reaches the reader falls steeply with the number of items, and the trigger that deepens retrieval for such questions fires on fewer than half of them.

evidence.detail: 55 aggregation retrieval losses (39 exclusive primary pattern); 37 of them not in list mode; all-gold-in-context 95.9% at one gold turn falls to 8.7% as n_gold grows; list mode fires on 39% of n_gold>=3 questions
evidence.method: measured (RET-1, RET-11) on the reference full run; trigger precision/recall is a CPU computation over the 1,540 rows

items.gap: B1 (aggregation retrieval) and I4 (list-mode trigger is an English regex): R14 adds the measured n_gold curve and the 37 missed-trigger questions. The 0-call trigger and the coverage objective are not built.
items.hypothesis: A trigger that combines question shape with the leg score profile fires on at least 70% of n_gold>=3 questions at no more than 15% false fire on single-gold ones; list-mode depth plus entity/session-diverse selection lifts all-gold-in-context for n_gold>=3 from 34% (non-list) to 50% or more, recovering 10-20 of 55 questions (about 0.6-1.3 points) without the cost of the slot loop.

solutions.name: Score-profile aggregation trigger
solutions.mechanism: Decide list-depth from question shape AND the retrieval score profile (flat top scores, many same-entity hits); no model call.
solutions.risk: false fire on single-gold questions adds distractors

solutions.name: Coverage-aware selection
solutions.mechanism: MMR-style selection with entity/session diversity so near-duplicates stop crowding the anchors.
solutions.risk: diversity can drop a true duplicate gold turn

solutions.name: Missing-slot second retrieval
solutions.mechanism: One bounded sufficiency check that names the missing slot, then exactly one targeted re-search (not the open slot loop).
solutions.source: IRCoT / Self-Ask [Trivedi2023-ircot] [Press2023-self-ask]; Mnemon ALL-need paging (R14-qry-2); EverOS sufficiency check (R14-hop-1)
solutions.risk: slot loop already measured net -3 at 8x cost; keep the bound

test.slice: fail_list (+ 60 matched n_gold>=3 correct as guard)
test.screen: S79 trigger + coverage (CPU first, offline over forensics); S80 second-retrieval bounded

expected_effect.label: hypothesis
expected_effect.text: 10-20 of 55 recovered (hypothesis); reader ceiling on cat1 given all gold is 75.5%, so recovery is capped at about 0.75 of the retrieval gain

items.title: Cross-session spread: turn-level, session-agnostic retrieval; summaries and episodes as legs
items.problem: Evidence for one question is spread over several sessions while retrieval is turn-level and session-agnostic; nothing asks whether each session that mentions the entity or topic is represented. Higher-grain units (session summary, episode, dated observation log) are the usual remedy, but the unit returned to the reader matters more than the quality of the summary text.

evidence.detail: 43 questions with gold in three or more sessions; all-gold rate 35.8% at 3 sessions and 15.5% at 4+; in-context accuracy 72.9% at two sessions, 62.5% at three

items.gap: B8 (sessions with no hit). R14 sharpens it to a per-session coverage objective and adds three engine ideas: render the parent summary next to each fact (MemOS background, Memori), return the parent unit with facts as keys (EverOS, Supermemory), and a dated always-in-context observation log without retrieval (Mastra OM).
items.hypothesis: A session-level leg followed by one best turn per matched session lifts all-gold coverage for n_sessions>=3 from 26% to 45% or more; rendering the parent summary line next to a hit adds context for 'which event' questions at under 200 tokens.

solutions.name: Per-session best turn after a session leg
solutions.mechanism: Session digest leg picks sessions, then one best turn per matched session joins the anchors.
solutions.cost: 0 at read; digest calls at session close (already built)
solutions.risk: digest hallucination; S33 fired zero calls so its inputs must be checked

solutions.name: Parent summary beside the hit
solutions.mechanism: Print the one-line parent episode/summary under each retrieved fact.
solutions.source: MemOS background field, Memori summary attach (R14-epi-1)

solutions.name: Dated observation log, no retrieval
solutions.mechanism: Background observer writes dated, prioritised observations that replace raw history; reader gets the log.

solutions.name: Summary degeneracy guard
solutions.mechanism: Reject looping summaries (<35% distinct 4-grams) and keep the previous one.

test.slice: fail_retrieval (b+cf) and fail_mix_120; metric distinct gold sessions represented
test.screen: S81 session_cover; S31/S33/S61 stay as queued

expected_effect.label: hypothesis
expected_effect.text: 43 questions in scope; expect 6-10 recovered if session coverage reaches 45% (hypothesis); overlaps M-1

items.title: Fusion and rerank cut loss: ranked gold discarded when legs are fused into a small pool
items.problem: Gold turns that one retrieval leg ranks well are dropped when the legs are fused into a small candidate pool (especially lexical-only or vector-only evidence that no other leg corroborates), and some survivors are dropped by a fixed keep-line while the token budget is half empty.

evidence.detail: 68 stage-b/cf fusion-cut questions plus 4 rerank-keep cuts; 11 of 15 top-10 cuts never entered the 20-pool; in-context rate 95.8% at best leg rank 4-10 falls to 67.9% at 21-30; 105 of 115 retrieval failures use under 3,000 of 4,096 tokens; 84 gold turns cut at fusion, 11 at rerank
evidence.method: measured (RET-4, RET-7, POS-2) from logged leg ranks to depth 60

items.gap: B7/B9/B10/I75/I78 are confirmed: protection stops at rank 3 per leg, fusion is rank-based, no fusion cut is logged. R14 contributes the rank-band table (best leg rank vs survival) that sizes a deeper protection value offline, and the convex-combination-versus-RRF question.
items.hypothesis: Protecting the top 8 per leg, fusing with score-normalised weights and letting the keep-line fill the token budget (about 15 anchors) keeps most of the 15 top-10 cuts and part of the 11-30 band, recovering 8-20 of 72 questions at zero model cost. Ceiling if every gold within depth 30 is kept: 20 questions.

solutions.name: Deeper per-leg protection
solutions.mechanism: Raise pool_protect_per_leg from 3 to 8 so BM25-top-10 or vector-top-10 gold survives fusion.

solutions.name: Score-aware fusion
solutions.mechanism: Convex combination of normalised scores instead of RRF k=60, calibrated on logged ranks.
solutions.risk: weights overfit to the dev conversations

solutions.name: Budget-driven keep
solutions.mechanism: Keep anchors until the token budget is filled (keep 15 or budget-driven) instead of a fixed 10.

solutions.name: Wider rerank pool
solutions.mechanism: Rerank 30-40 candidates, already queued as S67.

test.slice: fail_fusion (+95 lucky/barely cases as guard)
test.screen: offline CPU re-fusion from forensics first (no run); S82 protect8 + convex fusion; S83 budget keep; S67 queued

expected_effect.label: hypothesis
expected_effect.text: 8-20 of 72 recovered (hypothesis, upper bound about 20 within depth 30)

items.title: Lexical-zero and paraphrase gold: surface form is the strongest predictor of a miss
items.problem: Gold turns that share almost no content words with the question (paraphrase, synonym, category-versus-instance wording) are missed by both lexical and dense legs. Neither the stored record nor the query is enriched with the vocabulary of the other.

evidence.detail: 81 questions with gold turns of near-zero word overlap; word overlap is the strongest single predictor of a gold turn being found (embedding correlation about -0.48); 72 combined retrieval-stage questions are zero-overlap or BM25-miss with a vector hit

items.gap: B2/B5/B6/B15 confirmed. R14 adds the engine finding that most engines expand at write time (keys per fact), not at query time, and the literature view that query-time HyDE is net-neutral when a strong hybrid plus reranker is in place.
items.hypothesis: Document-side enrichment (generated question or instance-to-category terms per fact, filtered) lifts the no-leg answer-bearing gold turns; expect 6-8 of the 21 paraphrase questions. Query-side multi-query helps less than document expansion on this pipeline.

solutions.name: Document expansion at write
solutions.mechanism: Per fact, generate 2-3 questions it answers plus category words; filter with Doc2Query-minus; index with the fact.
solutions.cost: one batched call per fact set at ingest

solutions.name: Record-styled multi-search plus HyDE note
solutions.mechanism: Rewrite the question in the store's own wording (dated third-person) and add one invented answering note.
solutions.source: Mnemon planner, EverOS trio (R14-qry-1); HyDE [Gao2022-hyde]; Query2doc [Wang2023-query2doc]
solutions.risk: negative on strong hybrid; keep behind a guard slice

solutions.name: Learned sparse or late interaction leg
solutions.mechanism: SPLADE / ColBERT / BGE-M3 multi-functional leg alongside BM25 and dense.
solutions.cost: model inference at index and query

test.slice: fail_retrieval (81 ids, 21 paraphrase)
test.screen: S84 doc expansion; S76 paraphrase probes (OBS-GAPS); word_vector_leg on the 21 ids

expected_effect.label: hypothesis
expected_effect.text: 6-8 of 21 paraphrase questions (hypothesis); small share of the rest

items.title: Elliptical and context-dependent turns: decontextualisation and an index view
items.problem: Gold turns that are elliptical or anaphoric (a reply that carries the answer but not the topic) are unfindable because the topic lives in the neighbouring turn; a +-2 window around anchors reaches them only if the topical neighbour was itself found. Pronoun and plural referents are lost the same way.

evidence.detail: 32 context-dependent-gold questions (10 exclusive); 19 retrieval losses in sessions with a short-form window; elliptical turns about 10-15% of turns by the overlap rule
evidence.method: measured/heuristic (RET-6 overlap rule; OBS-03, OBS-09 measurements)

items.gap: A07/I6/B12 confirmed. OBS-GAPS already proposes write.index_view (S69) and write.restate_gate (S70); R14 adds exchange-pair records as a CPU-only alternative and the engine finding that window-fact arms lose on their own (S03 -4, S04 -6) because the returned unit matters.
items.hypothesis: Indexing exchange-level records (turn plus the turn it answers) as an extra leg, or a rule-built context prefix on the embedded text, recovers 8-10 of the 32 questions with no model call; LLM restatement only for rule-flagged turns adds 3-5 more.

solutions.name: Exchange-pair records
solutions.mechanism: Index each turn together with its addressed turn as an additional leg; return the pair.

solutions.name: Rule-built context prefix on embedded text
solutions.mechanism: Prepend speaker, session date and subject of the previous turn to the embedded text; content stays byte-identical.
solutions.source: Anthropic contextual retrieval [Anthropic2024-contextual-retr]; OBS-02 index view
solutions.risk: dilutes embedding if prefix too long

solutions.name: Gated restatement of flagged turns
solutions.mechanism: Rule score marks incomplete turns; one grounded call restates only those; grounding check drops invented words.
solutions.cost: 1 call per flagged window (10-15% of turns)

solutions.name: Day/session-first window boundary
solutions.mechanism: Cut windows at session or calendar-day change first.

test.slice: fail_retrieval + fail_context (OBS-GAPS)
test.screen: S85 exchange_records (CPU simulation first); S69/S70/S75 per OBS-GAPS

items.title: Indirect gold for judgement questions: evidence describes behaviour, never the question's words
items.problem: Open-domain (hypothetical or trait) questions ask for a judgement while the supporting turns describe behaviour; single-shot retrieval on the question text finds neither. The reader ceiling given all gold is also low.

evidence.detail: 28 open-domain retrieval losses with 47.6% of their gold turns missing; reader accuracy given all gold 46.9% on cat3 (96 questions); 41 open-domain wrong answers are not refusals

items.gap: B3 confirmed; the class open_domain_inference_retrieval has no built primary solution in the solution map. OBS-06 proposes inference probes (S74).
items.hypothesis: Rewriting the question into 3-4 evidence-kind sub-queries (what X chose, enjoys, said about A, B) recovers about half the missing gold (14 of 28), but the 47% reader ceiling caps the accuracy gain at 4-7 questions.

solutions.name: Evidence-kind query decomposition
solutions.mechanism: Planner emits sub-queries for the kinds of evidence that would settle the judgement.

solutions.name: Trait and preference synthesis at write
solutions.mechanism: Sleep-time profile/trait facts that give judgement questions a direct hit.
solutions.source: ours (profile_card_v2); Honcho peer card, Memobase profile

test.slice: fail_retrieval (28) + all 96 cat3; oracle-gold reader-only run first to size the ceiling
test.screen: S86 evidence_kind_probes; shares S74 probes (OBS-06)

items.title: Explicit-date questions: the date is treated as ordinary words, no session-date prior at fusion
items.problem: A question that contains an explicit calendar date points at the session of that date, yet the engine treats the date as ordinary words; the gold turn is found by one leg and lost in fusion. The temporal leg fires on few questions and is off in the reference.

evidence.detail: 13 failing of 180 explicit-date questions (167 pass as guard); 12 of 13 are fusion cuts with the gold session 0-12 days from the query date; temporal leg fires on 187 of 1,540

items.gap: B4/I8 sharpened: the loss is concentrated in explicit-date questions, not relative ones. Engine survey adds window overlap plus proximity boost inside the window instead of a hard span filter (Hindsight) and reference_time on every read (R14-time-2).
items.hypothesis: Boosting (not filtering) candidates whose session date is within a few days of the question date recovers 9-11 of 13 questions with no loss on the 167 passing ones.

solutions.name: Date-scoped retrieval prior
solutions.mechanism: Soft boost at fusion for candidates in sessions within N days of a date in the question.
solutions.source: ours (RET-3); Hindsight window overlap plus proximity (R14-time-3); TempRALM [Gade2024-tempralm]
solutions.risk: boost on the wrong year; keep soft

solutions.name: Explicit reference_time on every read
solutions.mechanism: Pass the conversation date, never the wall clock, to relative-phrase resolution.

solutions.name: LLM interval extraction for unsure phrases
solutions.mechanism: Rule first; one call only when the rule cannot parse.

test.slice: fail_temporal (13 fail + matched controls from the 180)
test.screen: S87 date_prior (CPU re-fusion first); S24/S62/S63 queued

items.title: Date and duration arithmetic done by the 9B reader; event dates lack precision and status
items.problem: Spans between two events, 'for N years' start dates and 'N months now' are answered by the reader's own subtraction; the wrong event line is picked for a 'when' question; a stored date does not say how precise it is or whether the state is still running.

evidence.detail: 19 date/duration reader failures; 15 how-long failures remain although every endpoint is annotated; 38 how_long/how_many-unit questions in scope; 10 pure arithmetic plus 8 wrong-event classes

items.gap: C5/I76/E05: R14 confirms the class is the best covered on paper and the least screened. Engine survey adds precision, status and type tags on the temporal pass (Mem0 platform) and a three-date line (Mastra).
items.hypothesis: duration_solve plus milestones on the 38 how-long/unit questions converts at least a third of the 15 in-context failures (5 questions, about 0.3 points) with zero model calls beyond endpoint extraction.

solutions.name: Deterministic date calculator
solutions.mechanism: Resolved event dates in, closed set of operations out (difference, ordering, N weeks before); code, not model.
solutions.cost: 0 (+1 call on about 5% for endpoint extraction)

solutions.name: Precision/status/type on event time
solutions.mechanism: Add precision (day/month/year) and ongoing-or-completed to the temporal envelope.

solutions.name: Fake-clock invariant test
solutions.mechanism: Guard that every replayed line carries its own timestamp, not the run date.

test.slice: fail_temporal date_* classes (19) + 38 unit questions
test.screen: S88 duration_solve + milestones (built-off, needs a screen only)

items.title: Over-refusal and premise denial: no typed commit route for judgement questions
items.problem: The reader answers 'not mentioned' or denies the premise when the evidence supports a committed inference (hypothetical, 'likely', world-knowledge hop). Prompt-only yes/no rules misfire on other question shapes, and abstention policy has no shared test.

evidence.detail: 40 over-refusal/premise-denial rows (26 cat3 failures); 14 open-domain refusals; 37 ungrounded rows overlap

existing: reader variants dated_infer / grounded_generic_infer / dated_world / routed
items.gap: C3 (yes/no rule rejected +5/-17) and C4 (screen pending) confirmed. R14 adds the gating principle: decide the route by code from the typed contract, not by prompt wording, plus the sufficiency-gated answer/infer/abstain literature and the shared-test finding that engines set abstention per engine.
items.hypothesis: Gating the commit route on the typed contract (yes/no, would/likely/might) keeps the C3 regression away and converts about one third of the 26 cat3 failures (+6 to +10 questions, 0.4-0.6 points) with no extra calls; a self-consistency vote on judgement shapes only (about 6% of questions) adds a few more.

solutions.name: Typed commit route
solutions.mechanism: Contract rule marks 'inference' shape; builder adds the commit-with-cited-line clause for that shape only; other shapes keep the unchanged text.

solutions.name: Sufficiency-gated answer/infer/abstain
solutions.mechanism: Three-way policy using a sufficiency verdict before answering.

solutions.name: Self-consistency vote on judgement shapes
solutions.mechanism: Three samples, majority, on judgement questions only.

solutions.name: Empty-context abstention without a call
solutions.mechanism: No context lines means abstain with no model call.

test.slice: fail_reader (40 + 25 refusal rows); guards cat5 and OP-Bench irrelevance
test.screen: S73 prompt, S74 probes (OBS-GAPS); S89 vote; S20 cat5 guard

items.title: Wrong detail and distractor use; one window size for every question shape
items.problem: The reader answers from a plausible sibling line: topical, near the gold line, but a different or generic detail. The distractor is a window neighbour of the gold in about a third of cases and a retrieval hit in over half. Context size is the same for every shape, so the window that helps temporal questions is paid for by single-hop distractors. Position effects (lost in the middle) do not reproduce at this context length.

evidence.detail: 46 wrong_detail rows, 59 distractor-source rows (19 window neighbours, 32 retrieval hits); accuracy given all gold falls 91% (<=40 turns) to 83.6% (>60 turns); position quintiles 0.89-0.92 (Fisher p=0.90) so no position effect; rank>3 gold 74.8% vs 90.8%
evidence.method: measured/heuristic (READ-2, DIST-1, LEN-1, POS-1, POS-2); 13 hand-confirmed

items.gap: C1/C9/R2-4/I6 confirmed: reordering was rejected, verification not screened, owner/event check not built. R14 adds the negative position result (do not spend a screen), the per-shape window, and Mastra/MemOS style attached source context.
items.hypothesis: A binding check that the cited line shares the question's event noun phrase and date (code), plus one repair call on mismatches, removes about a third of true distractor cases (+10 to +14 questions); a per-shape window (1/1 for non-temporal single-hop) recovers about 1 point on single-hop at no loss on temporal.

solutions.name: Provenance check (owner/event/date binding)
solutions.mechanism: Code checks the cited line against the question's head noun phrase and date; one repair call on mismatch only.

solutions.name: Quote-then-answer
solutions.mechanism: Reader quotes the line first; the quote must contain the head noun phrase.

solutions.name: Per-shape window and budget
solutions.mechanism: Narrow window for single-fact shapes, wide for temporal and multi-turn.

solutions.name: Evidence compression
solutions.mechanism: Compress distractor-heavy context before reading.

test.slice: fail_reader (46 + 59 ids); 2x2 narrow/wide window by shape on the dev slice
test.screen: S90 quote-then-answer; S91 window_by_shape; S92 verify_binding; S52-S54 queued

expected_effect.label: hypothesis
expected_effect.text: +10 to +14 (binding) and about +1 point single-hop (window), partly overlapping (hypothesis)

items.title: List and count completeness: partial lists, over-counted events, 'at least N'
items.problem: The reader returns one or two of several items, counts one event twice because it is mentioned on two dates, or hedges with 'at least N'. Retrieval of list members is handled; enumeration and de-duplication at read are not.

evidence.detail: 25 incomplete-list/wrong-count rows; 16 list_incomplete + 9 count_wrong; 7 of 9 counts are over-counts

items.gap: C6/I56 confirmed; the two_call and evidence-table variants have never been screened. R14 adds code-side counting from the model's listed events (PoT idea) and the enumerate-then-count shape.
items.hypothesis: An evidence table (one row per distinct event: actor, object, date) built by code from the context lines, followed by a count over the rows, fixes the over-count class (7 of 9) without the single-call collapse failure.

solutions.name: Evidence table, enumerate then count
solutions.mechanism: Code builds event rows; the model lists; a function counts and de-duplicates.
solutions.risk: collapse to one item (seen in count_verify)

solutions.name: Obligation coverage for list/count
solutions.mechanism: Evidence obligations name each required item before abstaining.

solutions.name: Contract-shaped output
solutions.mechanism: List shape prints one bullet per item; count prints number plus list.

test.slice: fail_list (25 + list/count-shaped controls)
test.screen: S93 evidence_table / two_call; S06, S11, S56 queued

items.title: Multi-turn join and multi-entity decomposition at read
items.problem: Questions that need two or more turns, especially across sessions or about several entities (intersection, difference, 'both'), are not joined by the reader even when all evidence is in context. Retrieval-side hop work is plentiful; reader-side decomposition with per-entity quotas and deterministic combine operators is not covered.

evidence.detail: 54 multi-turn reader failures (52 multi-session of 140 in-context); 43 multi-entity wrong answers; accuracy 90.0% at one evidence turn, 78.5% at two, 68.2% at three, 72.9% across two sessions

items.gap: New: reader-side decomposition when all evidence is already in context. Nearest existing: OBS-10 read.decompose_v2 (S77) for the retrieval side; the retired slot loop is not to be repeated.
items.hypothesis: Decomposition into per-entity sub-questions answered per turn and joined by code lifts multi-session in-context accuracy from 72.9% by +5 points (about +7 questions) at +2-3 calls on about 10% of questions.

solutions.name: Decompose then join
solutions.mechanism: Sub-questions per entity answered per turn; combine operators (intersection, union, difference, count merge) in code with entity quotas.

solutions.name: Evidence obligations join
solutions.mechanism: Join obligations stated before the answer.

solutions.name: Cross-session evidence table
solutions.mechanism: One table across sessions, one call.

test.slice: fail_list + new fail_multi (43, OBS-GAPS)
test.screen: S94 reader-side join (after S77); S56 queued

items.title: Ungrounded answers: new content words appear nowhere in the context
items.problem: The answer contains content words that occur in no context line (inference output, arithmetic result, world knowledge or fabrication). The diagnosed verification mode already flags such cases but is unscreened.

evidence.detail: 37 ungrounded wrong rows (22% of in-context wrong rows); 188 correct answers are also 'ungrounded' (false-defect risk)

items.gap: Confirmed: diagnosed mode flags 'a name no memory line contains' but has no screen. R14 adds the false-defect rate requirement.
items.hypothesis: slot_verify diagnosed repairs 1 in 4 of the 37 (+8 questions) at about 1.8% extra calls; without a gold, abstaining is the safe alternative on cat1-4.

solutions.risk: false defects on the 188 correct ones

solutions.name: Larger reader or thinking mode

items.title: Verbosity against a short gold: answer length follows difficulty, the lever is an output contract
items.problem: Wrong answers are enumerations or explanations many times the gold length. The length is a difficulty correlate (long answers follow refusals, lists and uncertain counts) so a length cap is not a fix; the lever is an answer-type contract that fixes the output shape per question type.

evidence.detail: 49 rows with answer/gold length ratio above 8

items.gap: Confirmed; no new screen needed beyond S06/S11 plus a report column.
items.hypothesis: Contract-fixed shapes (single fact one phrase; list bullet per item; count number plus list) lower the ratio>8 rate without lowering list recall.

solutions.name: Answer-type contract
solutions.mechanism: Output shape fixed per typed question shape.

items.title: Image captions: misattributed or photo-only evidence
items.problem: The answer is in an image caption but the reader uses a caption from another turn, or the gold fact exists only in the photo. Captions rendered inline in speech make ownership unclear; ingest-time description records are the common engine pattern, not read-time fetch.

evidence.detail: 6 caption-misuse rows (3 cross-turn mixing); 28 caption-only questions; 55 caption-decisive in OBS-05

items.gap: C7 (caption rule 85.8 vs 86.7, not adopted) confirmed. R14 adds the engine finding that Mem0, Hindsight, MemOS and EverOS describe images at ingest.

items.title: Speaker attribution: wrong-speaker answers are rare, but swapped-speaker golds penalise correct attribution
items.problem: Attribution by speaker is the right behaviour, yet in a set of questions the gold turn is spoken by the other person, so a system that ignores the named speaker gains and one that enforces it loses. Restatement can also erase who said it (speaker labels discarded).

evidence.detail: 1 reader-side wrong-speaker row; 39 speaker-swapped questions of which 23 are credited and not in the errata; 5 speaker candidates still to verify

items.gap: New: perspective features are scored against labels that sometimes contradict them; no stratum separates the 23 credited swapped-speaker rows.
items.hypothesis: Reporting the swapped-speaker rows as their own stratum explains any perspective-feature loss up to 1.5 points and prevents rejecting a correct attribution feature; owner tags stay tags, not filters.

solutions.name: Speaker-swap stratum in every report
solutions.mechanism: Report the swapped rows separately.

solutions.name: Per-speaker perspective ingestion
solutions.mechanism: Keep speaker as subject/owner on restated facts.

expected_effect.text: reporting fix; at most 1 question reader-side (hypothesis)

items.title: Judge false negatives after the date guard: superset lists, annotation equivalence, containment
items.problem: WRONG verdicts whose answer states the gold fact: a superset or concluding list, an equivalent annotation, a typo, containment with extra detail, a country/city or paraphrase pair, and relative-phrase golds the date guard does not parse. The judge is nearly deterministic, so these errors are systematic, not random.

evidence.detail: 23 false-negative rows by hand (10 clear, 4 likely, 9 borderline); central 16.6 (range 10-23); conventions v1/v2 reach only 6 of 14 clear/likely; 20 unparsed relative-phrase golds; 1,696 identical-answer groups across 6 runs with 4 flips
evidence.method: hand read of all 287 wrong rows (JUDGE-1, JUDGE-4, JUDGE-5)

items.title: Entity aliasing and link tables: seed-to-neighbour expansion without per-session LLM graph builds
items.problem: Names appear as nicknames, short forms, role words and typos, so entity-seeded legs are inert until aliases bind; multi-session evidence needs a hop from a seed hit to related stored items, but a graph built by an LLM per session is costly. String and embedding similarity alone mis-merge short names.

evidence.detail: 9 questions targeted by vocative/short-form binding (74 detected turns); entity leg inert until the graph arm builds entities; link expansion shares the 43 cross-session questions with M-2

items.gap: I54 confirmed and OBS-01 proposes write.vocative_alias_v2 (S68).
